reasons: Both versions pass all hard gates, but Version 2 demonstrates superior quality in soft criteria C3 (Things to do) and C1 (First minute) by fixing a critical gameplay frustration where escaping a burning car led to instant death, resulting in significantly higher job completion rates in testing. Version 2 also refines UI logic on the title screen and mobile controls, preventing new players from accidentally starting timed missions and reducing on-screen clutter.

Version 1 (v14) demonstrates superior stability in hard gate testing and includes critical quality-of-life improvements over Version 2, such as fixed police collision logic, context-sensitive mobile controls, and better onboarding restrictions that prevent new players from starting advanced modes prematurely.

Both versions pass all 10 hard gates and share the same city, art, and core systems. Version 2 (v14) edges ahead with the 'Second Car' release 2.2, which gives a meaningful gameplay improvement: an 8-second window after jumping out of a burning car where police hold fire, and police cars now pull up short of a player on foot instead of driving through them. This makes the chase loop more readable and survivable (measured: 0 of 8 cars wrecked at 3-4 stars vs 6-7 of 8 in 2.0.1). Version 2 also shows more transparent reporting of test failures and minor phone UI improvements (NITRO/RADIO buttons only when relevant). The frame rate dropped from 123 to 74 fps but still passes the G7 gate. Overall, v2's gameplay improvements slightly outweigh the frame rate regression.

Both versions pass all 10 hard gates and share the same core game (city, jobs, police, HUD, atmosphere). VERSION 1 (v14) adds the 'Second Car' mechanic and phone button optimizations, but these are marginal quality-of-life improvements rather than substantive new content; screenshots and overall feel are essentially identical.

Both versions pass all ten gates and share the same city, jobs and look, but Version 2 (release 2.2) is a strict incremental improvement: the courier shift is gated behind the first job for a cleaner first minute, the burning-car escape and fairer chases demonstrably work (3 of 3 jumps saved, far fewer wrecks at 4-5 stars), the phone HUD is decluttered, and its reporting is even more candid about flaky checks. The gains are modest but real across C1, C3, C4 and C5, giving Version 2 the edge.

Both versions pass all ten gates and share the same city, jobs and presentation, but Version 1 (release 2.2) measurably improves the soft criteria: police chases are more survivable and readable (burning-car escapes now work, 9/9 first-try Heat Wave runs vs 5/9, far fewer wrecks at 3-5 stars), the phone HUD is decluttered, and the title screen is simpler for a new player, with more honest test coverage; Version 2's only edge is a higher measured frame rate, which is negligible since both clear the 60 fps gate.
